transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Yeah, um… I came in because I’ve been making these small mistakes that are starting to feel really embarrassing, especially with things I thought I had double-checked. Like I’ll turn in an application or some research notes, and then later I notice there’s a skipped question or I mislabeled an artwork date or something like that.

It’s not like I don’t care about it—I really do check, or at least I think I do. That’s part of what’s frustrating. I’ll feel pretty sure I went over everything, and then some little detail is wrong anyway. It’s been happening enough that I started thinking maybe I should talk to someone, because it’s affecting things I’m trying to do and making me feel kind of stupid, honestly.
When you make these mistakes, do you find yourself having repeated, intrusive thoughts about them or feeling like you need to do something repeatedly to fix them?

Um… I don’t think so? Not in the sense of, like, a thought that keeps forcing itself into my head and then I have to do some exact thing to make it stop. I mean, I definitely feel embarrassed afterward and I’ll think about it more than I want to sometimes, especially if it was something I really should’ve caught. I’ll kind of replay it and be like, “How did I miss that?” But it feels more like frustration or worry after the fact, not like a repeated intrusive thought.

And I don’t think I do repeated fixing behaviors, exactly. I may go back and check something again if I realize I made an error, but it’s not like I have to check it a certain number of times or in a specific ritual way. It’s more just… I’m trying to make sure I didn’t mess it up again, if that makes sense.
Do you find it hard to stay focused on tasks, especially ones that require sustained mental effort, like reading through a long document or completing detailed work?

Yeah… definitely. That’s actually one of the bigger patterns I’ve noticed. If I know something is going to take real concentration, I’ll sort of avoid starting it, even if it’s important and even if I’m technically “working” on things around it.

Like, if I need to draft a curatorial proposal or read a dense theory chapter, I’ll suddenly decide I should answer emails, organize my desktop, wash a few dishes, look up some minor detail that isn’t urgent—basically smaller errands that feel productive but aren’t the thing I’m supposed to be doing. And then the main task just sits there, and I keep telling myself I’ll do it after this one small thing, and then after another small thing.

By the time I finally start, it’s often suddenly the night before it’s due, and then I’m stressed and rushing through something that probably would’ve gone better if I’d just started earlier. It’s not that I don’t care about the work. I do. I think part of the issue is that when I know it’s going to require sustained focus, it feels kind of mentally heavy before I even begin, so I end up circling around it instead of just doing it.
Have you noticed yourself feeling down, sad, or losing interest in activities that you usually enjoy, even things you used to look forward to?

Um… I’m not really sure I’d describe it that way. I mean, I get frustrated and kind of discouraged when I mess things up, especially if it feels like I should’ve been able to handle it, but I don’t think I’ve noticed a bigger, ongoing sadness exactly.

As far as losing interest, I don’t think so? I still care about the things I usually care about, and I still want to do them. Sometimes I might put things off or feel annoyed with myself, but it doesn’t feel like I don’t enjoy anything anymore. It’s more like I get stuck before doing things, not that I don’t want them or don’t care about them.
Over the past two weeks, have you felt down, depressed, or hopeless most of the day, nearly every day?

No, I don’t think so. I mean, I’ve had moments where I feel discouraged or kind of bad about myself if I’ve messed something up or fallen behind, but not like… most of the day, nearly every day.

It’s more situational, I guess. Like if something goes wrong, I’ll feel low for a bit, or frustrated, but I don’t wake up feeling hopeless every day or have that kind of constant depressed feeling hanging over everything. At least, that’s not how it’s felt to me over the past couple weeks.
Do you find yourself getting easily distracted by things around you, even during tasks that require your attention, like when you're trying to read or finish work?

Yeah, that happens a lot. Especially if I’m at my desk trying to read or write something that needs actual concentration. It doesn’t even have to be a huge interruption—like a siren outside, or someone talking in the hallway, or a door closing somewhere—and suddenly my attention is just… gone.

And then sometimes it’s not even something around me, it’s just a random thought. Like I’ll be reading and some idea about an exhibit or a way to arrange something visually pops into my head, and I’ll think, “Oh, I should just jot that down quickly,” but then that turns into looking something up, or sketching something, or opening another tab. And then twenty minutes later I realize I haven’t actually been reading the thing in front of me at all.

It’s frustrating because in the moment it feels like I’m still doing something related or useful, but when I come back to the original task, I’ve lost the thread and have to reread the same paragraph again. It’s like my attention gets pulled sideways really easily.
Have you noticed any days where you just feel emotionally flat or unable to feel pleasure, even in things you normally enjoy?

I don’t think so, not in the sense of feeling emotionally flat or like I can’t enjoy things. I mean, I definitely have days where I’m kind of tired or frustrated, and I might not get around to doing something I normally like, but when I do actually do it, I can still enjoy it.

Like, I don’t feel numb exactly. It’s more that sometimes I get stuck starting things, or I’m distracted, or I waste time and then feel annoyed with myself. But if something funny happens, I can laugh. If I’m doing something I’m interested in, I still care about it. I haven’t really noticed days where everything feels blank or pointless or like nothing can feel good.
Have you noticed any periods of time when you felt down or lost interest in things for several days in a row, even things you usually care about?

Not really, no. I mean, I’ve definitely had stretches where I’m frustrated with myself or kind of discouraged for a few days, especially if I feel like I’m behind on things or not doing what I meant to do, but I wouldn’t say I lose interest in everything I usually care about.

It’s more like I might put things off or feel annoyed, and then it can look from the outside like I’m not interested, but inside I still do care. If I actually get myself to do something I normally enjoy, I usually still enjoy it. I haven’t noticed a several-day period where I’m just down the whole time or where things I care about suddenly don’t matter to me.
